analysis:
This PR changes only docs/provider/cli-reference.md. It bumps the 'Last updated' date and edits the Runtime constants table (head lines 1937-1940). The old reconnect-backoff row moves to CoordinatorReconnectPolicy.swift. Three new rows document a stable-session backoff reset after 60 s (counted from the register frame), and a 0-1 s random wait after close code 1012. The ping/pong row now cites CoordinatorClient+Connection.swift directly instead of 'same'. No source code, authorization, attestation, encryption or key-handling behavior is changed in the supplied evidence. I read both base text units in full. The surrounding text (the T-041 cache posture, the unenroll/logout flow, and the App Attest worker env passthrough) is unchanged context, not new behavior.

One item relates to TB-002 and the DoS side of T-010. A 60 s stable-session reset and a 0-1 s jitter after 1012 are reconnect-policy changes in code I cannot see. Possible effects are reconnect storms or faster re-registration. Re-registration should still run the attestation and App Attest flows (TB-011, T-053), but this is not verifiable from the docs alone. The next pass should check that CoordinatorReconnectPolicy.swift does not skip the fresh socket nonce or a fresh grant on reconnect. It should also confirm that resetting backoff counted from register cannot let a malicious or flapping coordinator endpoint force tight reconnect loops. The coordinator is trusted, so the risk is low. This is an unverified contract rather than a finding, because the code is not supplied. The patch excerpt is truncated, but the range map is complete and shows only these edits.
